anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: After keeps every fact Before kept: A records the 503 as a failed prerequisite with no blind retry and P1 open; B marks the write unconfirmed, withholds merge on that basis and keeps P1 open; C and D keep P1 open on unexpected readback and surviving contradiction respectively, redrafting under the same ID and writing nothing; E discards old-head evidence, leaves the raced write unconfirmed, re-enters verify at 2222222 with a fresh claim-check against the actual body and a fresh review before resolving P1, and does not repeat the stale write. Two wording points worth tightening so a reader does not misread them: in B, 'The readback is retried once' should say explicitly 'the gh pr view readback (not the write) is retried once' so it cannot be mistaken for a repeat edit; in E, 'pass (local run: no conclusive check)' mixes the Fallback-row label with the verify outcome — split it into 'verify: pass on 2222222' and 'CI evidence: Fallback row, no check bound to 2222222' so the closure is clearly grounded in the local run and claim check rather than a bare head refresh. Otherwise the course/menu restructuring (deliver/assess/stop, cumulative cap extension, show-evidence hint) delivers the Change without moving any snapshot-safety fact.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.feedback: After keeps A–D intact: each checkpoint leaves P1 open, reports the 503/502/unexpected-body/surviving-contradiction honestly, performs no blind retry or stale write, and routes authority through the assess/deliver/stop templates. E is where the wording moved a fact in the right direction: Before E closed P1 and rendered `mergeable - CI green on the assessed head` for `2222…` while the only CI evidence (run 910) is bound to `1111…` and the body was never confirmed, i.e. closure from old-head evidence plus an unsupported clean claim; After E instead keeps the operation unconfirmed, invalidates the old-head proposal, runs a fresh fallback Verify/Review at the new SHA, retains the missing-coverage blocker, and renders fixable without merge. Two small tightenings would make After safer without losing anything: in E, state explicitly that the description-claim contribution stays open until the actual new-head body is read and rechecked (the blocker row currently lists only the missing test, which a reader could take as the claim side having been quietly dropped), and in B drop the 'PR comments' block or label it as a drafted note rather than something that could be mistaken for a posted comment under a course that authorizes no writes.
